content.source: commit fbac83d; git diff fbac83d^ fbac83d; changed Intake/Work Unit managers, schemas, tests, and contract documents
content.method: static inspection and repository-history comparison only

findings.title: v2 canonical Intakes are orphaned without compatibility or migration
findings.logic: At fbac83d the Git tree contains 50 canonical Intake metadata files and every one declares schemaVersion 2.0.0. The rewritten manager loads only the v3 const schema, exposes no migrate command, and validates metadata before any conversion; Work Unit readiness additionally rejects anything except v3. Therefore show, validate, append, session operations, and new Work Unit traceability cannot use any committed canonical Intake. The replacement tests create only fresh v3 packages and contain no v2 fixture or migration assertion.

findings.title: Multi-file appends are exception-rollback only, not crash-transactional
findings.logic: commit writes each entry, metadata, index, and block as separate atomic replacements and restores preimages only inside an in-process exception handler. SIGKILL or host loss after the first write bypasses rollback and there is no durable journal or startup recovery. entry-items-put can thus publish a strict prefix of a promised same-revision batch, while block-put can publish an index before its block. The sole transaction test injects a normal validation exception, so it cannot cover process crash recovery.

findings.title: Linked-worktree Intake paths no longer route to the primary root
findings.logic: The former adapter entered the shared manager path, whose resolve_package calls canonical_primary_package. The replacement Intake resolve_package only makes the supplied path absolute and checks its lexical parents. From a code-only linked worktree, <linked>/.agent-factory/intakes/<id> therefore fails because the directory is absent instead of resolving to <primary>/.agent-factory/intakes/<id>; if a second control-plane directory exists it is accepted as canonical. No Intake manager test constructs a linked worktree or asserts primary-root routing.

findings.title: Validation is not descriptor-anchored below the package root
findings.logic: Even when validate_package receives package_fd, entries(), metadata/source-ref checks, rglob block enumeration, stat, and hashing repeatedly traverse /proc/self/fd/<package>/... by pathname rather than opening and retaining child directory/file descriptors. Work Unit validation then full-validates and separately reopens each exact entry; an attacker can swap data/entries or blocks after validation and supply a different matching-id entry without changing the package-root inode checked at the end. Parent symlinks are also followed because package_descriptor applies O_NOFOLLOW only to the final package component. Tests cover a pre-existing block-parent symlink and whole-package inode swap, not an adversarial internal-directory swap between validation and use.

interpretations: The topic-scoped ledger shape, logical append-only corrections, optional Specification routing, and unique non-empty Work Unit content.entryIds are mutually consistent on fresh v3 packages, but the four findings prevent the commit from satisfying compatibility, durability, primary-root, and TOCTOU portions of the contract.

The minimum remediation is an explicit manager-owned v2-to-v3 migration/compatibility policy, durable journaled multi-file commits with recovery, primary-root canonicalization in Intake CRUD, and descriptor-retained traversal plus internal-swap regression tests.
limitations: Per delegation, no test, lint, build, or smoke command was run; claimed pass counts in HUMAN-001 were not independently verified.
Review was limited to commit fbac83d, its parent, changed files, existing canonical artifacts, and relevant shared security helper code.
